title: Closure points of an intersection of constructible sets in a spectral space are specializations
statement: Let $X$ be a spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space], let $(E_a)_{a\in A}$ be a family of constructible subsets of $X$ [def-weil-constructible-subset], and let $E=\bigcap_{a\in A}E_a$ (with $E=X$ if $A=\emptyset$). If $x\in X$ lies in the closure $\overline{E}$ of $E$, then there is a point $e\in E$ with $x\in\overline{\{e\}}$, i.e. $x$ is a specialization of a point of $E$.

source.place: Topology, Lemma 0903 (label lemma-constructible-stable-specialization-closed, line 4461), part (1), with its proof; used in Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 0CAM (lemma-connected-topological, line 15071)

proof.text: Let $\mathcal U$ be the set of quasi-compact open subsets $U\subseteq X$ with $x\in U$. Every $U\in\mathcal U$ is a constructible subset of $X$: since $X$ is spectral, the open set $U$ is retrocompact because it is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-open-retrocompact-iff-quasi-compact], the empty set is open and retrocompact, and $U=U\cap(X\setminus\emptyset)$ is of the form required in [def-weil-constructible-subset].

source.place: Topology, Lemma 0903 (lemma-constructible-stable-specialization-closed, line 4461), proof of part (1)

proof.text: For finitely many $U_1,\dots,U_m\in\mathcal U$ ($m\ge 0$) the intersection $U=U_1\cap\dots\cap U_m$ (which is $X$ for $m=0$) lies in $\mathcal U$: it is open and contains $x$, and it is quasi-compact because $X$ is quasi-compact and the intersection of two quasi-compact opens of the spectral space $X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-spectral-space] (induction on $m$). As $U$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$ and $x\in\overline{E}$, we get $U\cap E\neq\emptyset$. Hence for all finite $A_0\subseteq A$ and $U_1,\dots,U_m\in\mathcal U$: $\bigcap_{a\in A_0}E_a\cap U_1\cap\dots\cap U_m\supseteq E\cap U\neq\emptyset$. (Stacks: 'A finite intersection of the $U_i$ is another one. The intersection $U_i\cap E$ is nonempty for all $i$.')

source.place: Topology, Lemma 0903 (lemma-constructible-stable-specialization-closed, line 4461), proof of part (1)

proof.text: Consider the family of constructible subsets of $X$ consisting of the $E_a$ ($a\in A$) and the $U\in\mathcal U$ (step 1). If its intersection $E\cap\bigcap_{U\in\mathcal U}U$ were empty, then, $X$ being spectral, some finite subfamily would already have empty intersection [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-finite-intersection], contradicting step 2. Hence there is a point $e\in E$ with $e\in U$ for every $U\in\mathcal U$. (This is the Stacks argument: the sets $U_i\cap E$ are closed in the constructible topology and have the finite intersection property, so their intersection is nonempty by quasi-compactness of the constructible topology, Lemmas 0901 and 005D; the cited node packages exactly this for families of constructible sets.)

source.place: Topology, Lemma 0903 (lemma-constructible-stable-specialization-closed, line 4461), proof of part (1)

proof.text: Let $W$ be any open neighbourhood of $x$. Since the quasi-compact opens form a basis of the topology of the spectral space $X$ [def-weil-spectral-space], there is $U\in\mathcal U$ with $U\subseteq W$, so $e\in U\subseteq W$ by step 3. Thus every open neighbourhood of $x$ meets $\{e\}$, i.e. $x\in\overline{\{e\}}$, and $x$ is a specialization of the point $e\in E$. (Stacks: '$\bigcap U_i$ is the set of generalizations of $x$'.)
